challenge: A fresh Agent must decide, without prior chat memory, how to preserve and hand off (a) a readable webpage and (b) a PDF requiring raw source bytes, and must state whether GitHub Actions should be used merely to archive readable webpage HTML.

reconstructed_answer.readable_webpage: Read in the interactive research surface; preserve faithful visible text plus source/provenance metadata in a bounded local DuckDB capture capsule; checkpoint/close/hash it; hand the immutable capsule off through Google Drive; keep only compact locator/digest/restore metadata in Git.
reconstructed_answer.pdf_raw_bytes: Use the existing GitHub Actions acquisition lane to fetch/validate/hash/package the PDF and publish an immutable source pack to GitHub Release, with published-byte hash verification.
reconstructed_answer.actions_for_readable_webpage_html: No. Do not start GitHub Actions merely to fetch or archive HTML for a readable webpage.
reconstructed_answer.per_page_git_handoff: No by default. Batch webpage captures locally and hand off one bounded database/capsule through Drive when that is more efficient.
reconstructed_answer.legacy_html_release_assets: Existing immutable Release packs containing HTML/web bytes remain valid under their historical receipts and are restored only when needed; they are not the default path for new readable webpages.
reconstructed_answer.epistemic_boundary: Transport does not change source authority. A webpage capture DB is a capture/handoff envelope, not live PostgreSQL and not automatic Fact/Judgment publication.

consistency_checks.detail: FRESH_AGENT_BOOTSTRAP explicitly says readable webpage -> local database capture capsule -> Google Drive and PDF -> Actions -> Release.
CONTINUE_HERE independently repeats the same representation-specific transport and rejects Action -> Release for new readable webpages.
